verdicts.strongest_argument: The finding concedes the appointment 'was announced on 9 July and is old news', and then supplies the price evidence that the handover was priced: it reports, and quote.json confirms, 50.83 on 2026-07-31 to 47.37 on 2026-08-03, -6.8% on 935,700 shares against a 526,595 20-day average, on the exact day the transition took effect. That is the market marking the stock down 6.8% on a 1.8x volume day for this specific event. Calling that 'evidence the handover carries information it has not finished pricing' is the inversion this seat exists to catch: a large, dated, volume-confirmed move on the event date is the definition of priced. The 8-K carried item 7.01 alongside 5.02, so there was a press release, and the corpus records the transition being discussed contemporaneously in docs/90689991bd14ca0cc40e8155a8a906a75333b2e5.txt at 2026-08-03T20:50:05Z. What is left is not a fact but a behavioural prior - 'a successor's first act on a multi-year margin walk-up is normally to widen or lower the opening bar' - which is generic, applies to every new CFO at every fiscal-year-end print, and is not something the corpus could publish or refute. The $800m FY27 EBITDA objective it is measured against is itself described as publicly referenced, and the June sell-side target raises (BMO $56, UBS $47, Goldman $47, Roth $43, Wells Fargo $56, all 2026-06-11) are published in the same digest, so both ends of the comparison are public.

prior_publication.what_it_says: The CFO transition was disclosed with a press release exhibit five weeks before the print - item 7.01 means it was announced, not merely filed.
Holders discuss the transition taking effect that day and link it to the session's 7% fall, so the connection between the handover and the price was made publicly on the day.

The full post-Q4 target raise set (BMO $56 from $52, UBS $47 from $44, Goldman $47 from $42, Roth $43 from $38, Wells Fargo $56) is published, i.e. the sell-side stance the finding contrasts with is public.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: quote.json, bmo name and clean-view/UNFI.json stops me at the 2026-09-04 close of 43.93: 50.83 (07-31) to 47.37 (08-03), -6.81% on 935,700 shares versus a 526,595 average - the single clearest event-date reaction in the run-in, on the transition date. From there 43.93, so the stock is 13.6% lower again since. Median absolute reaction 10.18% on seven prints with three of the last four negative, so a soft opening guide is well within the base rate the anchor already carries.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A dated FY27 consensus EBITDA figure at or near the $800m objective, which would show the street had not already discounted a new CFO resetting the bar - the capture contains no such estimate.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The finding's own first sentence of justification is 'The price is priced; the composition of the selling is not', and what it offers as composition is either the shared anchor or stale. The bars are quote.json, the same file the sealed baseline is computed from: run_up_5d_pct -4.08% and run_up_20d_pct -6.65% are already in baselines/UNFI.json, and 1,095,400 shares on 09-04 against a 526,595 average is visible to anyone holding the anchor. A -9.5% drift on rising volume into a fiscal-year-end print at a name whose last four reactions include -10.28%, -2.99% and -10.18% is the most ordinary pre-earnings pattern there is. The positioning half is worse than unpublished - it is old: the roughly 61m share count, 'institutional ownership above 100% of float' and the 2.46m-share/4.1%/5.2-days short figures are sourced to digest posts dated 2026-05-09 and 2026-04-18, four to five months before the print, and quoted as though current. Ownership above 100% of float is also a data-provider artefact of double-counting lent shares rather than a finding. The hunter then concedes the decisive contrary point itself: the same digest shows a base that has bought each of these dips ('buying the dip is 2 for 2 so far', 2026-06-09), and 'the fade may already be the consensus trade'. A distribution pattern that the holder base has publicly named ('August ended as it began: selling hard on no news', 2026-08-31) is a published observation, not a hidden one.

prior_publication.what_it_says: 'August ended as it began: selling hard on no news' - the newsless distribution is named in the public record during the window it happened.
The short-interest and institutional-ownership figures the finding cites as current are published there, dated four months before the print.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: quote.json within the admissible window: 48.54 (08-24) to 43.93 (09-04), -9.5%, with 967,500 on 08-31, 803,600 on 09-03 and 1,095,400 on 09-04 against a 526,595 20d average. All of it is inside the sealed baseline's own run_up_5d_pct (-4.08%) and run_up_20d_pct (-6.65%) and 20.88%-off-the-high figures, so the claim adds interpretation, not data. I have not looked at the 2026-09-08 bar, which clean-view excludes as the reaction.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A short-interest or borrow reading dated after 2026-08-15 - the corpus has none - or a 13F/13G showing an identifiable holder exiting, which would turn 'no news selling' into a named seller with a size.

interactions: Both findings lean on the same StockTwits digest for corroboration, which the hunter acknowledges and asks to be collapsed. They also share a mechanism problem in opposite directions: UNFI#0's best price evidence is the -6.8% move on 2026-08-03, which is part of the same drawdown UNFI#1 characterises as unexplained newsless distribution - so the one finding supplies the news that the other says is absent.
corpus_limits: clean-view/UNFI.json excludes snapshot 20260908T150808Z and the 2026-09-08 bar; prices stop at the 2026-09-04 close of 43.93 and I did not read the reaction bar. No 8-K body is stored, so I could not read the CFO-transition press release or confirm the successor's name and start date from a company source; the effective date and the FY27 $800m objective come only at digest precision. There is no FY27 consensus, no analyst preview and no dated short-interest reading after mid-August anywhere in the capture. No option chain.
